overview.headline: Copying small DNA segments for lab analysis

keyPoints.point: The technique copies small segments for study
keyPoints.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyPoints.point: Studies of isolated pieces are nearly impossible without amplification
keyPoints.quote: studies of isolated pieces of DNA are nearly impossible without PCR amplification.

keyPoints.point: The method supports fingerprinting, detection and diagnosis of genetic disorders
keyPoints.quote: including DNA fingerprinting, detection of bacteria or viruses (particularly AIDS), and diagnosis of genetic disorders.

keyPoints.point: repeated denaturing and synthesis cycles yield many billion exact copies of original DNA
keyPoints.quote: is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times, leading to more than one billion exact copies of the original DNA segment.

keyTerms.gloss: small segments of genetic material copied by the technique
keyTerms.quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a technique used to "amplify" small segments of DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: enzyme that builds new DNA strands using original templates
keyTerms.quote: Next, an enzyme called "Taq polymerase" synthesizes - builds - two new strands of DNA, using the original strands as templates.

keyTerms.gloss: separates double-stranded DNA into single-stranded pieces when heated
keyTerms.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.

keyTerms.gloss: machine programmed to alter temperature for denaturing and synthesis
keyTerms.quote: It is directed by a machine called a thermocycler, which is programmed to alter the temperature of the reaction every few minutes
